case_scope.source_excerpt:
Fix a particle mass $m_p>0$ in kilograms and velocity space $V=\mathbb R^3$ with components in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The elastic collision set is
$$Q_{m el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in V^4:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}.$$
Thus each allowed event conserves momentum $m_p(v+w)$ and kinetic energy $m_p(|v|^2+|w|^2)/2$. Equip $Q_{m el}$ with the Borel sets generated by its relative topology.

Collision-rate data consist of a nonnegative, countably additive, $\sigma$-finite Borel measure $
u$ on these Borel sets. It is invariant under exchanging $v$ with $w$, exchanging $v'$ with $w'$, and exchanging the incoming pair $(v,w)$ with the outgoing pair $(v',w')$: for each of these maps $S$ and Borel set $E$, $
u(S^{-1}E)=
u(E)$. This is the three-dimensional physical restriction of the collision set and exchange conventions in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]], with $\sigma$-finiteness stated explicitly for the product integrals used by the entropy theorem. For physical applications of that weak identity, at a fixed position and time let $f:V	o(0,\infty)$ be the one-particle number density per spatial volume and velocity volume: $f(v)\,d^3v$ is number per spatial volume in the velocity element. Particle number is dimensionless, $d^3v$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-3}}$, and $f$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. A collision term $Q_
u(f)$, when a representative satisfying the absolutely convergent weak identity exists, has units $\mathrm{s^2\,m^{-6}}$, namely $f$ per second. Test functions $\varphi:V	o\mathbb R$ are measurable and have one common unit $U_\varphi$ for their values (dimensionless for the tests $1$ and $\log(f/f_{m ref})$, where $f_{m ref}>0$ has the units of $f$). Assign the measure $
u$ itself units $\mathrm{m^9\,s^{-7}}$: its numerical values are taken in these SI units, not as a density relative to an unstated measure on $Q_{m el}$. Thus $\int_V\varphi Q_
u(f)\,d^3v$ and the collision integral of $f^2$ times the test bracket both have units $U_\varphi\,\mathrm{m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$. The magnitude and distribution of $
u$ remain model inputs; dimensional consistency fixes neither a numerical collision rate nor existence of $Q_
u(f)$. The measure is a declared model input; no differential cross section or microscopic limit is inferred from this Definition.

supplier_interfaces.excerpt:
This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

supplier_interfaces.excerpt:
Fix $d\ge2$. The **elastic collision set** is
$$Q_{m el}:=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{4d}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\},$$
with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. A collision measure is a nonnegative countably additive measure $
u$ on this measurable space. It is symmetric if it is invariant under the exchanges $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(w,v)$, $(v',w')\leftrightarrow(w',v')$, and $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(v',w')$. These invariances are hypotheses on $
u$, not consequences of energy and momentum conservation.

Fix the velocity measure space $(\mathbb R^d,\mathcal L(\mathbb R^d),dv)$, where $dv$ is the Lebesgue set function of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]] and its countably additive measure-space structure is assumed as part of the data. This definition makes no existence assertion for that structure or for the collision operator. An input density is a finite-valued positive Lebesgue-measurable function $f:\mathbb R^d	o(0,\infty)$ whose four coordinate evaluations $f(v),f(w),f(v'),f(w')$ on $Q_{m el}$ are $
u$-measurable. Let $\mathcal D_
u$ be a declared set of such inputs. Put $\mathcal L^1_{m loc}:=\{q:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R:q	ext{ is Lebesgue measurable and }\int_K|q|\,dv<\infty	ext{ for every compact }K\subset\mathbb R^d\}$. Its elements here are chosen function representatives, rather than equivalence classes. A collision model includes a specified map $Q_
u:\mathcal D_
u	o\mathcal L^1_{m loc}$; write $Q(f):=Q_
u(f)$.

For $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, put $A=f(v)f(w)$ and $B=f(v')f(w')$. For a finite-valued complex Lebesgue-measurable function $\varphi$ on velocity space, put $\delta\varphi:=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$. Define the complete admissible test class $\mathcal T_f$ to consist of exactly those $\varphi$ for which $\delta\varphi$ is $
u$-measurable and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\varphi(v)Q_
u(f)(v)|\,dv<\infty,\qquad \int_{Q_{m el}}|(B-A)\delta\varphi|\,d
u<\infty.$$
Absolute integrability is in the sense of [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. The model also declares, for each $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, a complex linear testing subspace $\mathcal S_f\subseteq\mathcal T_f$ containing at least one nonzero test. Require the following **weak collision identity** for every $f\in\mathcal D_
u$ and every $\varphi\in\mathcal S_f$. A formulation adopting all admissible tests specifies $\mathcal S_f=\mathcal T_f$; a result using only particular tests names those tests and their linear span explicitly:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(v)Q(f)(v)\,dv= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(f(v')f(w')-f(v)f(w))(\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w'))\,d
u,$$
Both sides are absolutely convergent by the test-class definition. Admissible tests need not be bounded or compactly supported: $1$, velocity coordinates, squared speed, and $\log(f/f_{m ref})$ for a positive constant $f_{m ref}$ belong to $\mathcal T_f$ whenever they meet the displayed measurability and integrability conditions. A consumer invoking one of these tests must establish or assume those conditions and require it to belong to the declared testing domain $\mathcal S_f$. In particular, the entropy branch uses the span of $1$ and $\log(f/f_{m ref})$, with absolute convergence explicitly assumed. The map $Q_
u$, its input domain and its testing domains are adopted model data; the weak identity is their admissibility condition, not an assertion that every positive density and collision measure admit such a map or that these tests alone uniquely determine it. Molecular chaos or a microscopic derivation of the identity is not part of the definition.
